title: Largest Plus Sign in Binary Grid
description:
You are given an integer `n` representing an `n x n` binary grid initially filled with all `1`s, along with a list `mines` where each `mines[i] = [r, c]` sets cell `(r, c)` to `0`.

Return the **order** `k` of the largest axis-aligned **plus sign** of `1`s contained in the grid. An order-`k` plus sign centered at `(r, c)` consists of `grid[r][c] == 1` together with four arms of length `k - 1` extending up, down, left, and right—all containing `1`s. If every cell is `0`, return `0`.
constraints: All coordinates in mines are distinct.
hints: For every cell (r, c), the largest plus sign centered there has order equal to the minimum of consecutive 1s extending in each of the four directions: left, right, up, and down.

Initialize an n x n array dp with n everywhere (0 at mine coordinates), then sweep each row left-to-right and right-to-left and each column top-to-bottom and bottom-to-top updating dp[r][c] = min(dp[r][c], run).

examples.explanation: With a single mine at (4, 2) in a 5x5 grid, a plus sign of order 2 fits centered at (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3), etc., while no order-3 plus sign fits (center (2, 2) is blocked at (4, 2)).
Every cell of the 1x1 grid is a mine, so no plus sign exists (order 0).
With no mines in a 3x3 grid, the center (1, 1) forms an order-2 plus sign.
